title: Contain heterogeneous-context eviction spikes causing multi-deployment request blackouts
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Multiple customers (hosted, dedicated, and private deployments) have reported intermittent blackouts and P95+ P99 latency spikes during mixed-length workloads. Root cause appears to be coordinated KV-cache eviction events that perturb the admission/batching decision path and cause transient dispatcher stalls. This ticket consolidates the triage, cross-deployment mitigations, and a proposed code fix that introduces defensive admission pre-checks and a short-lived eviction backoff window to avoid synchronous churn.
acceptance_criteria: Repro case for mixed-length steady-state workload that triggers eviction spike is documented and runnable in CI
Dispatcher no longer experiences >5s stalls in canary after patch under synthetic repro (baseline: median stall 0.1s)
P95 token latency for impacted tenants returns to pre-incident baseline in Hosted/Dedicated/Private canaries
Feature flag to enable/disable eviction-backoff exists and defaults to OFF for Private until opt-in
New telemetry emits eviction-backoff events and admission-fail/retry reasons
investigation_notes: 2025-02-10 Aisha: initial customer-reported traces show synchronous KV eviction bursts coincident with long-context request arrivals; backlog amplification in dispatcher observed
2025-02-11 Liam: reproduced locally with mixed 32/4096 token workload; observed admission loop thrashing when multiple inflight batches trigger concurrent KV set operations
2025-02-12 Eng lead: heap of tickets aggregated across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; Dedicated tenants had amplified impact due to tenant-localized cache pressure
2025-02-13 SRE: network-level metrics show no infra loss; CPU/GPU utilization normal, pointing to runtime-level scheduling deadtime
2025-02-14 Bench: added microbenchmark showing eviction storm increases batch assembly time by 3-10x for short requests following long-context flush
proposed_fix: Add a short (configurable) eviction-backoff window and a non-blocking admission pre-check path: when a KV eviction event is in-flight, mark the pool as "evicting" for 100-300ms and route new short/latency-sensitive admissions through a fast-path that uses cached prefix slices or degraded KV metadata instead of forcing a synchronous eviction. Also implement an admission hysteresis counter to avoid repeated immediate re-admissions for the same tenant. Provide a runtime flag and a safe default: enabled in Hosted/Dedicated by default, opt-in for Private deployments.
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag and enable for internal canaries (hosting and dedicated staging clusters)
Run 48h canary with synthetic mixed-length traffic and real traffic shadowing (SLO watcher on)
If canary stable, roll to 10% of Hosted production and 1 dedicated tenant; monitor eviction-backoff events and latency regressions
Full rollout after 7-day stability window and sign-off from SRE and Product
For Private customers: provide config toggle and a migration guide; recommend enabling after on-prem upgrade to runtime-1.20
qa_plan: Automated repro integrated into CI (kitchen) that runs mixed-length load for 10k requests and asserts no stall >500ms
Add unit tests around admission pre-check fast-path and eviction flag transitions
Manual validation: run convergence test on a dedicated cluster with bursty long-context traffic and confirm no P99 regressions
Security perf review to ensure no data leakage when using degraded KV metadata path
risk: Medium: changes touch admission/scheduling paths and KV-cache lifecycle. Danger areas are functional correctness of degraded fast-path and any unintended priority inversion under extreme load.
